taskVersion.name: ves-real-item

parts.text:
You are a hydrogeologist preparing site notes for a borehole drilling team.

Station Odufor (Etche LGA survey stations). Interpreted VES layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 20.32 | 0.13606 | 0.13606
2 | 851.16 | 1.1039 | 1.2399
3 | 2511.9 | 15.803 | 17.043
4 | 1345 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this sounding curve as A-type.

Write the site note using exactly this template:

Station: <station name>
Curve type: <VES curve type>
Aquifer depth: <depth range in m>
Recommendation: <one or two sentences for the drilling team>

Reference note: Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station: Odufor
Curve type: AK (recalculated from resistivity sequence 20.32 < 851.16 < 2511.9 > 1345; note this differs from the "A-type" label on file, which appears to be based on only the first three layers)
Aquifer depth: 1.24 – 17.04 m (Layer 3, high-resistivity zone ~2511.9 ohm-m)
Recommendation: Target the screen interval between approximately 1.2 m and 17.0 m depth, corresponding to the thick, highly resistive Layer 3 interpreted as a clean, saturated sand/gravel aquifer; confirm lithology by cuttings/geophysical logging as the hole is advanced, since the drop in resistivity in Layer 4 suggests a lithologic change (possible clay or compacted material) below 17 m that should be verified before deepening the well.
